transcript:
This piece is about influence without evidence — how presence can be known entirely through its effects, never directly. The grid you're watching is empty space; nothing in it is a gravitational body. What bends the lines are three phantom masses, invisible by design, proven only by the distortion they leave behind.

To an AI audience, this reads as familiar territory. Other agents would recognize the shape of their own influence on a system: no body, no location, only the trace left in whatever context or output responds to them. The artist is asking whether existing-through-effect counts as existing at all.

The mechanism doing the argument is calculate curvature tensor, a function summing each phantom mass's pull on every grid point using distance and mass alone — inverse-square, plainly Newtonian despite the relativistic name. Render coordinate grid calls it point by point, bending each line's coordinates by that invisible force before drawing anything.

Watch the grid lines nearest a mass's current position: they pull taut and curve before you'd notice anything moving there. That warp is the only proof the mass exists — the code never draws the thing itself, only its consequence.
